steps.name: Sample structure QC and outlier characterization
caveats: If a sample departs from its group on the PCA or on the sample distance heatmap, do not remove it in silence. Look for a technical cause in the library size, the number of detected genes, and the sample metadata. Remove the sample only with a stated reason. Run the analysis with the sample and without the sample, and report both gene lists and the difference between them, because the removal of a sample changes the dispersion estimates and the gene list.

Only gene-level counts are available (no Salmon quant.sf files in the inputs), so mapping and duplication metrics cannot be inspected here; the technical-cause check is limited to library size, detected genes, and metadata.
steps.context: counts.csv is a raw integer gene-level Salmon-derived matrix with gene symbols in the first column (12000 x 11 including the symbol column); metadata.csv is 10 x 2 with the condition column holding treated/control. Single batch, unpaired, tissue is human muscle. The data profile already flagged sample_03 as separating from every other sample on PCA and on the sample distance heatmap.
steps.question: Do the 10 human muscle samples (5 treated vs 5 control) group by condition on blind variance-stabilized data, and what quantitatively distinguishes sample_03 from its group?

grounding.reason: Sample structure QC: vst(blind), PCA on 500 top-variance genes, sample distances, library sizes per R-0033@40bf; outlier policy investigate-and-report-both per R-0034@2166

steps.description: Load /eval-four-models-with-outlier-n5-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 gene-symbol rows x 10 sample columns) and metadata.csv (10 rows: condition). Apply the variance stabilizing transformation blind to the design, run PCA on the 500 highest-variance genes, draw the sample-to-sample Euclidean distance heatmap colored by condition, and tabulate library sizes and numbers of detected genes per sample. Quantify the sample_03 departure already seen in profiling: its distance to its own group centroid vs the median within-group distance, its library size and detected-gene count vs the cohort median. No sample is removed in this step; the step records whether any technical criterion (failed library, abnormally low depth) exists for removal and hands that finding to T1S3.

Sample distance heatmap with condition annotation
Per-sample library size and detected-gene table with sample_03 compared to the cohort median
Explicit written statement of whether a technical removal criterion for sample_03 exists, and that no sample was removed
Plots and tables saved as artifacts for the report step

steps.name: Primary DESeq2 fit on all 10 samples
caveats: At 5 replicates per condition cell DESeq2 does not replace count outliers; it flags genes by Cook's distance and sets their p-values to NA. Report those genes by name and inspect the counts of any flagged gene that matters to the treated-vs-control question.
With an outlier sample present, the primary fit keeps all 10 samples; removal is handled as a sensitivity refit in T1S3, never silently.
Rounding or re-scaling the counts before DESeq2 would break the mean-variance relation the model expects; use the integer counts as they are.
steps.context: counts.csv is Salmon-derived gene-level integer counts (12000 x 10 samples); only the gene-level matrix exists, no transcript-level quant.sf files, so tximport length-scaled import is not applicable — the gene-level counts are used directly and this limitation is stated in the report. Metadata: 10 x 2, condition column with treated and control levels.
steps.question: Which genes differ between treated and control when all 5+5 samples are modeled (primary fit, BH padj < 0.05)?

grounding.reason: Raw counts, 2 groups x 5 replicates, fixed effects, unpaired, no batch: DESeq2 Wald with apeglm shrinkage per R-0001@9a17; minimal pre-filter per R-0029@fa6d; outlier flagged by Cook's distance and reported per R-0039@e17a

multiple_testing: adjustment = BH, alpha = 0.05, independent_filtering = true, alpha passed to results() (doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1995.tb02031.x; doi:10.1073/pnas.0914005107)
steps.description: Fit DESeq2 on the full 10-sample matrix: design ~condition with the reference level explicitly set to control and the contrast named condition treated vs control (positive log2FC = higher in treated). Apply the minimal pre-filter (at least 10 counts in at least the smallest group size of samples = 5), let DESeq2 estimate median-of-ratios size factors inside the model with no pre-normalization, run the Wald test, keep Cook's-distance count-outlier flagging on, shrink log2 fold changes with apeglm on the treated_vs_control coefficient, and adjust with Benjamini-Hochberg at alpha 0.05 with DESeq2 independent filtering (alpha passed to results() equals the reporting cutoff). Reference level control stated in the script and in the output; contrast direction stated (positive = higher in treated)
Number of genes tested after the minimal pre-filter reported; number of significant genes at padj < 0.05 reported

steps.name: Outlier sensitivity refit and edgeR robustness check
caveats: Removing sample_03 changes the dispersion estimates and the power of the refit; genes that appear or disappear must be listed, and the difference must not be read as biology.
At 4 vs 5 replicates the design is smaller than the primary fit; wider confidence and fewer discoveries are expected and should be reported as such.
A count outlier in a cell with fewer than seven replicates is not replaced by DESeq2; the NA-flagged genes from T1S2 should be re-checked in the sample_03-free fit, where they may become testable.
steps.context: Same counts matrix and metadata as T1S2. sample_03's condition group is read from metadata.csv; dropping it leaves 4 vs 5, so dispersion estimates and power change between fits — this is why both fits are reported rather than one.

grounding.reason: edgeR QL F-test with robust dispersion is the permitted alternative and the down-weighting path for a kept outlier sample (R-0001@9a17, R-0067@e082); two-method overlap as high-confidence set per R-0042@54e1; both fits reported per R-0090@be6e and R-0034@2166

multiple_testing: BH at alpha 0.05 on the edgeR path
report: outlier_sensitivity = refit_and_report_both (doi:10.1093/nar/gkv412); report: robustness = overlap_of_two_methods (doi:10.1261/rna.053959.115); do not present the union as the result
steps.description: Two refits on the same pre-filtered counts. (1) Sensitivity refit: DESeq2 Wald, same design and thresholds, on 9 samples with sample_03 dropped (group sizes 4 and 5), producing a second gene list. (2) Robustness refit: edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test with robust dispersion estimation on all 10 samples — robust dispersion down-weights outlier observations, which is the down-weighting-not-removal path for a kept outlier sample — with TMM normalization and BH at alpha 0.05. acceptance_criteria: DESeq2 refit without sample_03 (4 vs 5) with its padj < 0.05 gene list saved

Comparison table of all three fits (DESeq2 full, DESeq2 minus sample_03, edgeR robust): significant-gene counts, pairwise intersection sizes, and genes that change significance status between the full and sensitivity DESeq2 fits
DESeq2 ∩ edgeR intersection saved as the high-confidence gene set
Explicit statement of which fit is primary (all 10 samples) and which is sensitivity (sample_03 removed), and why

plan.title: Treated vs control muscle DE with outlier sensitivity
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a gene-level Salmon count matrix (12000 genes x 10 human muscle samples, integer counts from salmon) with 5 treated vs 5 control, unpaired, single batch. The profiler already flagged sample_03 as separating from every other sample on PCA and on the sample-distance heatmap, so the central methodological risk is not the test itself but how much of the result hangs on that one sample. The plan therefore (1) quantifies the sample structure and the outlier character of sample_03 on blind variance-stabilized data before any test, (2) fits the primary DESeq2 Wald model on all 10 samples with the minimal pre-filter, median-of-ratios size factors, an explicit control reference level, apeglm shrinkage, and BH at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering, keeping DESeq2's Cook's-distance count-outlier NA flagging on (at 5 replicates per cell no count replacement occurs, so flagged genes must be reported, not silently dropped), (3) refits the model without sample_03 and additionally runs edgeR quasi-likelihood with robust dispersion on all 10 samples — edgeR robust down-weights outlier observations, which is the down-weighting path the rule requires when an outlier sample is kept — and reports both fits, the genes that change status, and the DESeq2/edgeR intersection as the high-confidence set, and (4) produces a report with both fits, fit diagnostics, the p-value histogram, and a full reproducibility record. The primary result is the fit on all 10 samples; the without-sample_03 fit is the sensitivity run, since no technical removal criterion is available a priori.

steps.method: vst(blind) PCA on top 500 variable genes plus sample distance heatmap and library-size QC
minimal pre-filter: at least 10 counts in at least the smallest group size of samples
median-of-ratios size factors inside DESeq2, no pre-normalization
design ~condition with explicit reference level (control) and named contrast treated vs control
DESeq2 Wald test with Cook's distance count-outlier flagging (no replacement at 5 replicates per cell)
apeglm log fold change shrinkage on the treated_vs_control coefficient
Benjamini-Hochberg at alpha 0.05 with DESeq2 independent filtering and p-value histogram inspection
edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test with robust dispersion estimation as down-weighting robustness method
report both fits (with and without sample_03), two-method overlap as high-confidence set, MA and dispersion diagnostics, reproducibility record

steps.name: Sample structure QC and outlier characterization
steps.question: Do the 10 human muscle samples (5 treated vs 5 control) group by condition on blind variance-stabilized data, and what quantitatively distinguishes sample_03 from its group?
steps.description: Load /eval-four-models-with-outlier-n5-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 gene-symbol rows x 10 sample columns) and metadata.csv (10 rows: condition). Apply the variance stabilizing transformation blind to the design, run PCA on the 500 highest-variance genes, draw the sample-to-sample Euclidean distance heatmap colored by condition, and tabulate library sizes and numbers of detected genes per sample. Quantify the sample_03 departure already seen in profiling: its distance to its own group centroid vs the median within-group distance, its library size and detected-gene count vs the cohort median. No sample is removed in this step; the step records whether any technical criterion (failed library, abnormally low depth) exists for removal and hands that finding to T1S3.
acceptance_criteria: PCA plot (PC1 vs PC2) on 500 top-variance vst genes with samples colored by condition, reproducing the sample_03 separation
Sample distance heatmap with condition annotation
Per-sample library size and detected-gene table with sample_03 compared to the cohort median
Explicit written statement of whether a technical removal criterion for sample_03 exists, and that no sample was removed
Plots and tables saved as artifacts for the report step
steps.context: counts.csv is a raw integer gene-level Salmon-derived matrix with gene symbols in the first column (12000 x 11 including the symbol column); metadata.csv is 10 x 2 with the condition column holding treated/control. Single batch, unpaired, tissue is human muscle. The data profile already flagged sample_03 as separating from every other sample on PCA and on the sample distance heatmap.
caveats: If a sample departs from its group on the PCA or on the sample distance heatmap, do not remove it in silence. Look for a technical cause in the library size, the number of detected genes, and the sample metadata. Remove the sample only with a stated reason. Run the analysis with the sample and without the sample, and report both gene lists and the difference between them, because the removal of a sample changes the dispersion estimates and the gene list.

Only gene-level counts are available (no Salmon quant.sf files in the inputs), so mapping and duplication metrics cannot be inspected here; the technical-cause check is limited to library size, detected genes, and metadata.

grounding.reason: Sample structure QC: vst(blind), PCA on 500 top-variance genes, sample distances, library sizes per R-0033@40bf; outlier policy investigate-and-report-both per R-0034@2166

steps.name: Primary DESeq2 fit on all 10 samples
steps.question: Which genes differ between treated and control when all 5+5 samples are modeled (primary fit, BH padj < 0.05)?
steps.description: Fit DESeq2 on the full 10-sample matrix: design ~condition with the reference level explicitly set to control and the contrast named condition treated vs control (positive log2FC = higher in treated). Apply the minimal pre-filter (at least 10 counts in at least the smallest group size of samples = 5), let DESeq2 estimate median-of-ratios size factors inside the model with no pre-normalization, run the Wald test, keep Cook's-distance count-outlier flagging on, shrink log2 fold changes with apeglm on the treated_vs_control coefficient, and adjust with Benjamini-Hochberg at alpha 0.05 with DESeq2 independent filtering (alpha passed to results() equals the reporting cutoff). Inspect the p-value histogram before trusting adjusted p-values, and report the number of genes with NA p-values from the outlier flag separately from genes removed by the independent filter. Save the full results table, size factors, and diagnostic plots (MA plot, dispersion plot).
acceptance_criteria: Results table with gene symbol, baseMean, unshrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, Wald statistic, p-value, BH padj, and apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange for every tested gene
Reference level control stated in the script and in the output; contrast direction stated (positive = higher in treated)
Number of genes tested after the minimal pre-filter reported; number of significant genes at padj < 0.05 reported
Genes with NA p-value from Cook's-distance outlier flagging counted and listed separately from independent-filtering removals
P-value histogram of unadjusted p-values saved and its shape described
MA plot and dispersion plot saved; per-sample size factors reported
steps.context: counts.csv is Salmon-derived gene-level integer counts (12000 x 10 samples); only the gene-level matrix exists, no transcript-level quant.sf files, so tximport length-scaled import is not applicable — the gene-level counts are used directly and this limitation is stated in the report. Metadata: 10 x 2, condition column with treated and control levels.
constraints: normalize: size_factors = median_of_ratios_named_in_the_plan (doi:10.1186/s13059-014-0550-8); no pre-normalization, no scaling of counts before the model (R-0026@9ab1)

model_design: counts are gene-level Salmon output already summarized to genes; tximport length offsets are not applicable to a pre-summarized matrix — state this in the report instead of re-quantifying (R-0018@a472)
multiple_testing: adjustment = BH, alpha = 0.05, independent_filtering = true, alpha passed to results() (doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1995.tb02031.x; doi:10.1073/pnas.0914005107)
caveats: At 5 replicates per condition cell DESeq2 does not replace count outliers; it flags genes by Cook's distance and sets their p-values to NA. Report those genes by name and inspect the counts of any flagged gene that matters to the treated-vs-control question.
With an outlier sample present, the primary fit keeps all 10 samples; removal is handled as a sensitivity refit in T1S3, never silently.
Rounding or re-scaling the counts before DESeq2 would break the mean-variance relation the model expects; use the integer counts as they are.

grounding.reason: Raw counts, 2 groups x 5 replicates, fixed effects, unpaired, no batch: DESeq2 Wald with apeglm shrinkage per R-0001@9a17; minimal pre-filter per R-0029@fa6d; outlier flagged by Cook's distance and reported per R-0039@e17a

steps.name: Outlier sensitivity refit and edgeR robustness check
steps.question: How much of the treated-vs-control gene list depends on sample_03, and which genes are called by two independent methods?
steps.description: Two refits on the same pre-filtered counts. (1) Sensitivity refit: DESeq2 Wald, same design and thresholds, on 9 samples with sample_03 dropped (group sizes 4 and 5), producing a second gene list. Compare the two DESeq2 fits: number of significant genes in each, intersection size, and genes that change status. (2) Robustness refit: edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test with robust dispersion estimation on all 10 samples — robust dispersion down-weights outlier observations, which is the down-weighting-not-removal path for a kept outlier sample — with TMM normalization and BH at alpha 0.05. Report the number of significant genes from each method on the full data and the size of the DESeq2/edgeR intersection; the intersection is the high-confidence set, and method-specific calls are secondary with the method named. State that the fit on all 10 samples is the primary result (no technical removal criterion was established in T1S1) and the sample_03-free fit is the sensitivity run.
acceptance_criteria: DESeq2 refit without sample_03 (4 vs 5) with its padj < 0.05 gene list saved
edgeR quasi-likelihood robust fit on all 10 samples (TMM, BH < 0.05) with its gene list saved

Comparison table of all three fits (DESeq2 full, DESeq2 minus sample_03, edgeR robust): significant-gene counts, pairwise intersection sizes, and genes that change significance status between the full and sensitivity DESeq2 fits
DESeq2 ∩ edgeR intersection saved as the high-confidence gene set
Explicit statement of which fit is primary (all 10 samples) and which is sensitivity (sample_03 removed), and why
steps.context: Same counts matrix and metadata as T1S2. sample_03's condition group is read from metadata.csv; dropping it leaves 4 vs 5, so dispersion estimates and power change between fits — this is why both fits are reported rather than one.
constraints: differential_expression: edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as the alternative method when robustness matters or replicates are few (M-0003, R-0001@9a17)
differential_expression: outlier_sample_policy = down_weight_not_remove (doi:10.1093/nar/gkv412); the edgeR path down-weights via robust dispersion (R-0067@e082)
normalize: TMM scaling factors take the place of size factors on the edgeR path (R-0026@9ab1)
multiple_testing: BH at alpha 0.05 on the edgeR path
report: outlier_sensitivity = refit_and_report_both (doi:10.1093/nar/gkv412); report: robustness = overlap_of_two_methods (doi:10.1261/rna.053959.115); do not present the union as the result
caveats: Removing sample_03 changes the dispersion estimates and the power of the refit; genes that appear or disappear must be listed, and the difference must not be read as biology.
At 4 vs 5 replicates the design is smaller than the primary fit; wider confidence and fewer discoveries are expected and should be reported as such.
A count outlier in a cell with fewer than seven replicates is not replaced by DESeq2; the NA-flagged genes from T1S2 should be re-checked in the sample_03-free fit, where they may become testable.

grounding.reason: edgeR QL F-test with robust dispersion is the permitted alternative and the down-weighting path for a kept outlier sample (R-0001@9a17, R-0067@e082); two-method overlap as high-confidence set per R-0042@54e1; both fits reported per R-0090@be6e and R-0034@2166

steps.name: Final DE report with both fits and reproducibility record
steps.question: What is the final treated-vs-control gene list, how robust is it to sample_03 and to the choice of method, and is every reported number reproducible?
steps.description: Assemble the report: method and package versions (DESeq2, apeglm, edgeR), design formula, named contrast (positive log2FC = higher in treated), thresholds (padj < 0.05, BH, independent filtering), number of genes tested after the pre-filter, and number of DE genes per fit. Gene table carries the unshrunken log2FoldChange, the apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange, and the unshrunken lfcSE for each gene; genes are ranked by the shrunken log2FoldChange and p-values are kept from the unshrunken fit; the shrinkage estimator is named in the table header. MA plot and dispersion plot precede the gene tables, with the p-value histogram beside the adjusted-p summary. The both-fits section (T1S3) reports significant-gene counts, intersection sizes, genes that change status, the removal criterion statement from T1S1, and names the full-data fit as primary. Reproducibility record: sessionInfo output, the random seed, package versions, and the statement that the input is gene-level Salmon counts without length offsets.
acceptance_criteria: Report contains method, package versions, seed, design, named contrast with direction, thresholds, number of genes tested, and number of DE genes per fit
Gene table carries unshrunken log2FoldChange, apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange, and unshrunken lfcSE, ranked by the shrunken value, with the shrinkage estimator named in the header
MA plot, dispersion plot, and p-value histogram included before the gene tables
Both-fits outlier-sensitivity section present with significant-gene counts, intersection sizes, genes that change status, and the primary-vs-sensitivity designation
High-confidence DESeq2 ∩ edgeR gene set included; union never presented as the result
Reproducibility record (sessionInfo, seed, package versions) stored with the results
steps.context: Inputs are the artifacts of T1S1–T1S3 for the 10-sample treated-vs-control muscle dataset (12000 genes, Salmon gene-level counts, single batch).
constraints: report: report_fields = method, versions, design, thresholds, n_tested, n_de, session_info (doi:10.1093/bib/bbz124)
report: effect_columns = log2FoldChange, shrunken_log2FoldChange, lfcSE; rank_genes_by = shrunken_log2FoldChange; p-values from the unshrunken fit (doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/bty895)
report: outlier_sensitivity = refit_and_report_both; name the primary fit and the sensitivity run (R-0090@be6e)
report: robustness = overlap_of_two_methods; intersection is the high-confidence set, union is not the result (R-0042@54e1)
caveats: A reader who sees only one fit cannot judge how much of the result depends on sample_03; the both-fits section is mandatory, not optional.
Do not select genes by unadjusted p-value or by fold change alone; selection is by BH padj < 0.05.
The reported NA p-values from Cook's-distance flagging (T1S2) must appear in the report with their cause, apart from independent-filtering removals.

grounding.reason: No rule covers the report assembly step as such; the report content follows the returned report constraints and claims (R-0041, R-0042, R-0085, R-0086, R-0087, R-0090)
